$comment: %FULL% for Thunderbird. %NOTE% Generated by build.mjs from src/ports/thunderbird.json, which drops this $comment from the output: Thunderbird checks a theme manifest against a closed schema and refuses an unknown key as a corrupt file. Do not edit ports/thunderbird/. Install: zip the flavour folder's two files (manifest.json and theme.css) into an .xpi (the release attaches one per flavour), then Tools > Add-ons and Themes > the gear menu > Install Add-on From File, and enable it under Themes; Thunderbird does not require add-ons to be signed (xpinstall.signatures.required is false in its greprefs.js), so the unsigned file installs and stays installed. To try a change without packaging, Tools > Developer Tools > Debug Add-ons > Load Temporary Add-on and pick this manifest.json. Nothing is renamed or made executable. Installing a rebuilt .xpi over the theme does nothing unless its version is higher, so bump %VERSION% or remove the theme first. Verified on Thunderbird 157.0.1 only; strict_min_version is 128.0, and anything below 157 is unverified. Thunderbird ignores a CSS variable it no longer defines, so a later release that renames one loses that surface and nothing else. No environment is needed. The theme_experiment block sets Thunderbird-only CSS variables on the root of every chrome document; their names are mapped under theme_experiment.colors and their values sit in theme.colors beside the native keys. Palette names appear only for structural chrome: surface0 is the field, button and calendar-toggle fill and Thunderbird's second layout surface, surface1 the hairlines, field borders, pressed or hovered fill, folder total count and third layout surface, surface2 and overlay0 the fourth layout surface and the two stronger border steps, crust the calendar's weekend shading and surface0 its today column, on a weekend too (Thunderbird's own today, mantle, sits 1.9 to 2.7 from crust in OKLab x100 on Mire and Blackwater; surface0 and crust are 4.21 apart or more in every flavour and tint), surface1 the calendar's week pill. --color-gray-70 is mantle and --color-gray-50 surface1, as Catppuccin sets them: both are raw tokens Thunderbird builds many greys from, and repainting them is what carries the palette into surfaces no variable names. theme.css, the experiment's stylesheet, reaches the calendar's mini-month, which declares its colours on its own element where a root variable cannot reach; it names no colour, only the variables set here, and its selector outranks Thunderbird's light-theme block. Its day numbers are tint, accent as readable text, on a ui.background box. --lwt-frame is set to the frame colour because Thunderbird 157 paints the top toolbox and the status bar with it but its theme engine only sets --lwt-accent-color, so without it both bars fall through to the white native window, under every theme including Thunderbird's own dark one. Deliberately left unset: accentcolor and textcolor (deprecated aliases of frame and toolbar_text), ntp_background and ntp_text (Thunderbird has no new-tab page), the spam, tag, read-status and flag colours (Thunderbird's own status colours, which no role covers), the message body (web content the theme cannot reach), the Settings tab (preferences.xhtml is the one document Thunderbird does not mark lightweightthemes, so no theme reaches it), the every-other-row stripe in old-style lists such as the calendar's event list (the system colour -moz-oddtreerow, near white on Wisp and a step off the background on the dark flavours; a theme stylesheet cannot select ::-moz-tree-row), and the unfocused selected row (--listbox-selected-bg), which wants a ui.selection.inactive role that does not exist yet. Host-owned pairings, measured with lib/color.mjs contrast() as Wisp / Fen / Mire / Blackwater: Thunderbird derives --selected-item-color from sidebar_highlight and mixes it into the card background itself (10/15/15% light, 15/20/25% dark) under ui.text: current 9.21 / 7.71 / 10.99 / 12.40, selected 8.60 / 7.19 / 10.35 / 11.73, selected and current 8.60 / 6.71 / 9.70 / 10.99; the same colour fills primary buttons under sidebar_highlight_text (ui.on.fill, build-checked); the new-mail dot (tint, not text) on a current card 4.18 / 4.57 / 5.61 / 6.45; the folder-pane unread count is ui.on.badge on ui.badge (build-checked), and a collapsed folder draws the same ui.badge as outlined text on the pane, 3.98 / 4.14 / 3.82 / 3.97, held to 3:1 as a component; in the mini-month, days are tint on ui.background, 4.75 / 5.55 / 6.56 / 7.46, other-month days ui.text.muted and week numbers ui.text.subtle on ui.background (build-checked), today ui.text on surface1, 6.23 / 6.10 / 10.70 / 11.70, and a selected day ui.on.fill on ui.fill (build-checked); in the calendar views, the week pill is ui.text on surface1 (the same 6.23 / 6.10 / 10.70 / 11.70), weekend text ui.text on crust (build-checked as ui.pane.tertiary), and the drag box ui.text on ui.selection, 7.66 / 6.60 / 9.29 / 10.57. Thunderbird also reads --color-gray-70 as its light-scheme icon and toggle-border colour, where mantle is 1.12:1 on Wisp; the mini-month and folder counts, the two places that showed it, have their own variables, and any other place it shows needs the same. Differs from Catppuccin (catppuccin/thunderbird, branch main, commit 0289f3bd): the tab strip, frame and Spaces bar are ui.pane.tertiary and the toolbar ui.background, not base and mantle; sidebar_highlight and popup_highlight are ui.fill under ui.on.fill, the row-selection meaning Thunderbird gives them, not the accent under mantle; toolbar_field_highlight is ui.selection under ui.text, not the accent; toolbar_field_border_focus is ui.focus, because Thunderbird draws every focus outline with it; the message list and cards are ui.background on a ui.pane.secondary pane, not crust and mantle; layout colours, unread, new-mail and link colours are set, where Catppuccin leaves Thunderbird's own; the new-mail subject is ui.text (already bold), because tint falls to 3.90 on Wisp and 3.98 on Fen on a selected card; --ab-cards-list-bg and --in-content-box-info-background are dropped (gone from Thunderbird 157) and so is the empty styles.css reference; Thunderbird reads --color-gray-70 and --color-gray-50 as a surface in dark mode and as text in light mode, and gray-50 as both in one scheme, so Catppuccin's token values alone leave the mini-month days at 1.12:1 on Wisp and other-month days at 1.31:1 on Mire: the mini-month goes through theme.css and the folder counts and layout steps through their own variables; the calendar's weekend, today-on-weekend, week pill, selected day label and drag box are palette colours, where Thunderbird uses its own blue and ink; the unread and new-mail counts are both ui.badge, where Thunderbird uses grey and blue; --button-primary-* and --lwt-accent-color are left to Thunderbird, which already derives them from sidebar_highlight and frame.
